- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early and then drops too sharply, missing subsequent mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, particularly when true values show upward momentum.
- Forecast exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical mean is below 85.
- Model reacts too aggressively to recent price drops, underestimating recovery or overcorrecting downward.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the middle of the 30-day window, especially after volatility spikes.
- When true values show strong downward momentum, model often fails to recognize it, continuing to forecast upward.
- Model overestimates volatility in the final 5 days, leading to overcorrection or overshoot after sharp declines.
- Forecast often fails to capture the “mean reversion” effect after sustained high prices, leading to prolonged overestimation.
- Model tends to underestimate prices when true values are clustered near the 30-day moving average, especially in the last 10 days.
